prompt: Original educational conceptual illustration, landscape 3:2. Warm ivory paper, sophisticated hand-painted gouache/watercolour, confident fine brown outlines, navy lettering, restrained teal, coral and amber. Editorial science illustration with spacious composition and large legible labels. The explanatory structure must carry the meaning visually: molecules, objects, geometry or flow; never paragraphs in boxes. No organs, regional anatomy, teeth or joint cutaways, tissue layers, invented histology, diagnostic photographs, radiographs or patient data. All symbols are explicitly conceptual. Footer: 'Conceptual teaching model • Not to scale'. Title 'A pattern that resolves by morning', subtitle 'Typical growing pains'. Left under a large moon labelled 'Evening / night': a PAIR of soft slippers, both surrounded by small coral ache sparks, label 'Both legs may ache'. Broad rightward time arrow leads to right under a sun labelled 'Morning / day': a pair of trainers with light motion lines and a ball, no pain sparks, label 'Pain settles; normal activity'. This is a time-pattern analogy using footwear, no legs or bones. A clearly separate narrow bottom strip with small red flag icon says 'Reassess if: morning pain • limp • swelling • unwell'. No suggestion that all nocturnal pain is benign, no growth plate illustration.

teaching.question: Which features fit typical growing pains, and which should prompt reassessment?
teaching.answer: Bilateral evening or night aches that settle by morning with normal daytime activity fit the usual pattern. Morning pain, limping, swelling or systemic illness need reassessment.

title: A pattern that resolves by morning
caption: Typical growing pains affect both legs in the evening or night and settle by morning. Morning pain, limp, swelling or systemic illness require reassessment rather than automatic reassurance.
alt: Moon and sunrise panels compare paired slippers with ache sparks at night and active shoes by day; a separate red-flag strip lists atypical features.

review.notes: Both night slippers have ache marks; morning trainers and ball show normal activity without pain. The rightward arrow and night/day labels agree. Red-flag strip explicitly calls for reassessment with morning pain, limp, swelling or being unwell. No bone-growth mechanism or organ/joint anatomy invented.
